title: Access to Information and the Teacher's Role as a Filter Between Essential Information and Noise
keywords: access to information|teacher role|information filtering|digital skills|digital educational technologies|artificial intelligence in education|responsible AI use|plagiarism avoidance|referencing|information overload|children and adolescents|interdisciplinary projects
abstract: In contemporary society, access to information has become significantly simpler, and the spread of information occurs rapidly. In the past, information was monopolized by educational institutions and religious organizations. However, this unlimited informational access has led, especially among children and adolescents, to perceptual errors regarding the world they live in. This has been caused by their lack of ability to filter the vast quantity of information they are exposed to. The teacher is a generator of knowledge who works daily with both a vast amount of concepts and numerous students. In the digital era, the teacher must interpret information, filter it, and finally transmit it to students. It is particularly important for the teacher to possess advanced digital competencies and to understand that digital educational technologies represent a vital resource that contributes to more efficient communication with students, as well as to increased creativity and the accumulation of new knowledge. Artificial intelligence applications must be managed properly by the teacher—not by forbidding their use, but by encouraging students to use them responsibly, for the purpose of learning and personal development, without promoting plagiarism. The teacher can promote the use of artificial intelligence in the development of interdisciplinary projects assigned to students, with the stipulation that students must first be educated to cite the sources they access and to learn how to recognize fake information.

title: Fine-Tuning Large Language Models for Multi-Task Consumer Data Analysis in Fashion Design Process
keywords: large language models|RoBERTa fine-tuning|fashion design process|consumer data analysis|sentiment analysis|topic classification|market analysis|pricing practices|fashion education|digital transformation
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly growing within the fashion industry, with current attention primarily focused on image transformation and generation. However, the application of text comprehension AI in design processes, particularly in market research, remains insufficiently explored. This research fine-tunes RoBERTa models to construct an analytical framework including data cleaning, sentiment analysis, and topic classification for Chinese women's fashion analysis.The research analyzed 30,796 user comments from Bilibili. The fine-tuned models achieved strong performance: 95% accuracy for data quality classification, 97.65% for sentiment analysis, and F1-scores ranging from 0.70 to 0.97 across nine topic categories.Analysis of 6,029 high-quality comments revealed that 89.1% of consumers expressed negative or neutral sentiments, with size fit (43.5%) and gender differences (41.3%) being main concerns. The research identified nine systematic industry challenges, including size standards deficiencies, design practices that enforce traditional gender norms at the expense of functionality, and unfair pricing practices.This research shows that fine-tuning Large Language Models works for fashion processes analysis, providing evidence for widespread consumer dissatisfaction. The research fills the gap in applying fine-tuned LLMs to fashion design processes while demonstrating new ways for integrating fashion education with AI, contributing to digital transformation in fashion education and industry development.

title: DIGITIZATION AND THE USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN EDUCATION AND THE LABOR MARKET IN ROMANIA
keywords: artificial intelligence in education|digitization of education|higher education|Romanian higher education|digital skills|algorithmic bias|data security|ethical considerations|university administration|AI policy|responsible AI deployment|Romania
abstract: This article attempts to analyze current trends in digitization as well as the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in education, with a focus on the higher education system in Romania. The present study synthesizes recent literature, European and international policies, and national strategic programs, providing practical examples of how new digital technologies are being integrated into teaching and assessment by faculty. Opportunities for student learning are also discussed, as well as the streamlining of administrative processes, the development of digital skills, and associated risks such as ethical concerns, data security, algorithmic bias, and dependence on external providers. The final part of the article includes illustrative tables and graphs regarding the evolution of digitization in educational institutions, as well as a comparative study between international best practices and the current Romanian context. Finally, the article proposes a series of public policy recommendations and university practices suitable for a responsible and sustainable implementation of AI in the Romanian academic environment for both students and faculty.

title: The Rise of AI Tools in Classrooms: Threat or Opportunity for Academic Integrity
keywords: artificial intelligence in education|academic integrity|academic dishonesty|AI-generated content detection|intelligent tutoring systems|assessment practices|ethical challenges of AI|student awareness|responsible AI adoption
abstract: Purpose: The rapid integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into education has transformed learning by enhancing personalisation, efficiency, and accessibility. However, it has also raised concerns about academic integrity. This study examined the ethical implications, benefits, and risks of AI use in classrooms, focusing on learning processes, assessment practices, and student behaviour. Methodology: A systematic literature review was conducted using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) framework. Peer-reviewed studies published between 2014 and 2025 were retrieved from Google Scholar, SpringerLink, and Scopus. Forty-one eligible articles were critically analysed to identify the educational benefits and ethical challenges associated with AI tools. Results: The findings indicate that AI technologies, including intelligent tutoring systems and generative writing assistants, enhance learning outcomes, engagement, and instructional efficiency. However, they also raise ethical concerns by blurring the distinction between legitimate academic support and misconduct while complicating the detection of AI-generated content. Inconsistent institutional policies and limited student awareness further increase the risk of academic dishonesty. Novelty and Contribution: This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of the ethical challenges surrounding AI in education and explains how AI adoption reshapes academic values, accountability, and integrity. It offers original insights into balancing technological innovation with ethical educational practices. Practical and Social Implications: The findings guide educators, policymakers, and technology developers to establish clear ethical guidelines, strengthen institutional policies, and improve student awareness. These measures can support the responsible integration of AI while preserving academic integrity and maintaining trust in educational assessment.

title: REVOLUTION IN LEARNING: INTEGRATION OF AI TOOLS INTO HIGHER EDUCATION — BIBLIOGRAPHICAL ANALYSIS
keywords: generative AI in education|AI tools|higher education|ChatGPT|personalized learning|student motivation|academic integrity|critical thinking|research trends|higher education quality
abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence, particularly generative AI tools, has significantly influenced higher education systems worldwide. In recent years, scholarly attention has increasingly focused on the educational potential of these technologies as well as on their ethical, institutional, and pedagogical implications. The aim of this paper is to identify key research trends and thematic areas related to the integration of artificial intelligence tools in higher education through a bibliometric analysis. The study is based on a dataset of 51 empirical articles indexed in the Web of Science database and published between 2021 and 2025. Data analysis and visualization were conducted using the VOSviewer software. The results reveal a substantial increase in research output after 2023, largely driven by the widespread adoption of generative AI tools such as ChatGPT. Major research themes include personalized learning, student performance and motivation, as well as issues related to academic integrity and critical thinking. The findings confirm the interdisciplinary nature of the research and indicate a shift from initial scholarly discussions to a more systematic examination of the impacts of artificial intelligence on the quality of higher education.

title: Toward Fair and Ethical Teacher Evaluation: A Qualitative SLR on AI-Enhanced Value-Added Approaches
source_name: Proceedings International Conference on Business Economics & Management
keywords: teacher evaluation|value-added models|generative AI|knowledge tracing|algorithmic bias|educational equity|assessment fairness|student self-regulation|cultural fairness|teacher anxiety|bias correction|AI transparency|human-centered AI
abstract: AbstractThe rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into education has reshaped how student learning is monitored and how teachers are evaluated, raising new questions about fairness, ethics, and equity. This qualitative systematic literature review synthesizes findings from 24 empirical and conceptual studies to examine how Value-Added Models (VAM), knowledge tracing techniques, and generative AI (GenAI) tools are being integrated into teacher evaluation systems. The review identifies three dominant themes: (1) persistent validity and bias concerns in traditional VAMs, particularly regarding socioeconomic status (SES), cultural differences, and missing data (Chetty et al., 2014; Rothstein, 2010); (2) the emerging role of machine learning and autoregressive knowledge tracing models in improving prediction accuracy and capturing students’ self-regulated learning behaviors (Piech et al., 2015; Zhou et al., 2025); and (3) the ethical implications and equity risks associated with AI-enhanced assessments, including AI trust, cultural fairness, and teacher anxiety (Kong & Yang, 2024; Tossell et al., 2024). The synthesis highlights that while AI-enhanced VAM frameworks show promising improvements, with reported accuracy gains of 5–12% and bias reductions to under 5%, there is limited qualitative evidence on how teachers, students, and school leaders perceive these systems. The review proposes a human-centered, ethically informed framework that integrates GenAI transparency, SRL behavioral indicators, and bias-correction mechanisms to support fair teacher evaluation. Future research should employ cross-cultural qualitative designs to examine how AI-driven evaluation tools function in diverse school contexts and to ensure alignment with UNESCO’s global education equity agenda.

title: How Artificial Intelligence may influence therapeutic adherence
keywords: artificial intelligence|medication adherence|nursing practice|machine learning risk prediction|chatbots|digital coaching|chronic disease|hospital readmission|algorithmic bias|digital health literacy|patient autonomy|nurse-patient relationship|remote patient monitoring|patient education
abstract: Background. Therapeutic non-adherence affects approximately half of all patients with chronic conditions and is a leading driver of preventable morbidity, hospital readmission and excess healthcare expenditure. As nurses are positioned at the front line of patient education, monitoring and follow-up, the rapid emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) tools has direct relevance for everyday nursing practice. Objectives. To synthesize current evidence on how AI-based solutions, including machine-learning risk-prediction models, conversational agents, smart pill devices and tailored digital coaching, may influence therapeutic adherence, and to discuss the implications for contemporary nursing practice. Material and methods. A narrative review was conducted using PubMed, CINAHL, Scopus and Web of Science. Studies published between 2017 and 2025 addressing AI applications in medication or treatment adherence were selected, with priority given to systematic reviews, randomized clinical trials and nursing-relevant evidence. Results. AI-based interventions improved medication adherence by approximately 6.7% to 32.7% compared with usual care in randomized trials. Predictive models identified high-risk non-adherent patients with an area under the curve up to 0.87, allowing earlier and better- -targeted nursing interventions. Conversational agents enhanced patient engagement and self-management in chronic conditions such as diabetes, hypertension and heart failure, while reducing readmissions by up to 25% in some studies. Persistent barriers include data quality, algorithmic bias, digital health literacy and ethical concerns about patient autonomy and confidentiality. Conclusions. AI offers a meaningful opportunity to support nurse-led adherence strategies through earlier risk identification, personalized education and continuous remote monitoring. To realize its potential, nurses require structured training in digital health, professional standards must address ethical and legal aspects, and AI tools should be designed as a complement to, not a substitute for, the therapeutic nurse-patient relationship.
